content.comment_body: I'm a bit confused about the compatibility of the basic module I recently purchased: [product_name] - [article_no]. Here is a voltage class compatibility table: [url] There's also a module/expansion compatibility note, but I can't find [article_no] basic module listed. Does this mean it's incompatible with all modules, or compatible with all? [url] Is there a matrix or table showing compatibility between any basic module and expansion module?

Why do you think it's not listed? You have [product_name] and it's in the table. This just shows compatibility between older and newer series [article_no]. Summary: Expansion modules with article numbers ending in [article_no] or [article_no] cannot be used with [version_no] modules. Only expansion modules ending in [article_no] are compatible with [version_no]. This has been the case since the first [version_no] released in 2014. With your [product_name], you can use all related expansion and analog modules if their article number ends with [article_no]. However, 230V expansion modules are not compatible.

Thank you. By the way, can I use all 24V expansion modules if my logic module is supplied with 24V? For example, can I connect [product_name] modules ([article_no], [article_no]) and power both the logic and expansion modules with 24V?
Each expansion module requires its own power supply.
Sorry, it's still not clear to me. Can I power a 24V module and a controller (12/24) with a single 24V supply line for both devices, or not?
Is the circuit diagram unclear? One power supply is enough for both the controller and expansion modules.

The circuit is clear and shows that only one supply is needed for both the controller and expansion modules. But my question remains: can 12/24V and 24V units be mixed, using a single 24V power supply line? For instance, can I connect a [product_name] expansion module to a [product_name] controller and use a single 24V supply? Sorry if my question seems unusual. Thanks in advance

I'm still having trouble understanding your question as the diagrams make it clear. 12/24 VDC base and expansion modules can run on 12 VDC or 24 VDC. Modules designed specifically for 24 VDC cannot use 12 VDC. If you are still uncertain, I'm not sure how else I can assist.

Let me clarify with a diagram. If I have a mix of 12/24VDC, 24VDC, and 24VDC/AC units (controller and expansions), can they all operate together when powered at 24VDC? Simply put, can all three configuration examples work (see attached diagrams 1, 2, and 3)?

It seems you still don't understand: 12/24 VDC modules: Supply can be 12 VDC or 24 VDC. 24 VDC modules: Supply must be 24 VDC. 24 VDC/AC modules: Supply can be 24 VDC or 24 VAC. What do all three have in common? 24 VDC. Now is everything clear?

So now it's clear: all 12/24VDC, 24VDC, and 24VDC/AC modules can be powered by 24VDC. Therefore, all three of my diagram examples work. A simple table listing the controller on one axis, expansion on the other, with X marks for compatible options would make things clearer. Thanks for your time.
Why is that? It's just a matter of understanding what 12/24 VDC, 24 VDC, and 24 VDC/AC mean. These are basic concepts.

So now it's clear: all 12/24VDC, 24VDC, and 24VDC/AC modules can be powered by 24VDC, and all three diagram setups will work. A simple table matching controllers and expansions would be clearer. Thanks for your time. If you had checked the manual, you would have found a table with all possible combinations. Helpers can't always know every detail from user questions. If you're starting out, it's best to study the manuals. Don't worry and keep reading! Regards, [user_name]
But that table doesn't explain that you can use the same 24 VDC supply for every combination of base and expansion modules.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are struggling to understand compatibility between different types and generations of [product_name] modules, specifically around the use of 12/24VDC, 24VDC, and 24VDC/AC power requirements. There is confusion over whether a single 24V supply can be used to power different combinations of controllers and expansion modules and how article numbers affect compatibility. The documentation provided by [company_name] is seen as insufficiently clear, leading to repeated questions and clarifications within the thread.

They are seeking practical tables or diagrams that visually present which modules and configurations work together, and how they can be powered using a single supply line.
